card.name: Lavani
card.era: Traceable to the 1560s; flourished under Peshwa rule (18th-19th c)
card.profile: Lavani is a popular genre of song and dance from Maharashtra, combining traditional song with dance performed to the beats of the dholki drum and noted for its powerful rhythm (Wikipedia). Female performers wear nine-yard nauvari saris and dance to quick-tempo songs that address society, religion, politics and romance, often with erotic or satirical overtones (Wikipedia). It has two main streams - the philosophical Nirguni Lavani and the sensual Shringari Lavani - and developed into public Phadachi Lavani and intimate Baithakichi Lavani; it has been central to Marathi folk theatre (tamasha) (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Patronized by Maratha lords and prominent during late Peshwa rule, Lavani originally served as entertainment and a morale-booster for soldiers, and many performers come from Maharashtra's Mahar, Kolhati and Matang communities (Wikipedia).
